steps.name: Port the cross-stop echo dedup into per-stop assembly, both surfaces
steps.proof:
DEFECT THE ENGINE'S JUDGES CAUGHT (twice, independently): the de-dup port rebound composed_by_stop to the POST-dedup grouping before finish() built the trace, which (a) turned the fail-closed guard `if final_sentences != source_sentences: raise` into a TAUTOLOGY (both sides were the same stop_idx filter over the same list) and (b) recorded post-dedup text as CompositionTrace.source_sentences/source_payload_sha256 under derivation='provider_response' while response_sha256 still named the RAW body — so on any tour where de-dup dropped a sentence the certification artifact claimed bytes the provider never sent.

ROOT CAUSE OF THE DEFECT: the step's own test asserted `trace.source_sentences == shipped` and justified it, in a comment AND a docstring, as 'FinalTourBlueprint requires a trace's cited source sentences to equal the stop's FINAL sentences'. That justification is FALSE. artifact.py:764-770 computes `tuple(item.source_sentences[i] for i in item.source_sentence_indexes)` and compares THAT to the final sentences — it indexes INTO source_sentences — and CompositionTrace's validators (artifact.py:395-412) require those indexes to be monotonic, unique, in-range and one-per-final-sentence. The model was always built for a SUBSEQUENCE. An independent judge re-derived this and confirmed it before this step was marked done.

FIX: composed_by_stop stays the RAW provider payload; the tautology is replaced by a real subsequence proof (monotonic cursor per stop, raising when a final sentence is absent from that stop's raw provider output — which catches a glue/reflection line with a mis-echoed stop_idx being re-attributed) recording the surviving indexes; plus a full-attestation guard refusing any sentence that ships covered by no trace. NOT NEW CHECKS, and this matters for D3: before A5, composed_by_stop already held the raw payload, so the original strict-equality guard already refused both cases. These two guards are the minimal generalization that preserves that same strength under de-dup.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, verbatim:
  [A] re-inject the rebind -> `E AssertionError: stop 1's trace must attest the RAW provider payload, not the post-dedup text: source_payload_sha256 is read as 'what the provider returned', and response_sha256 already names that same untouched body` (1 failed in 0.08s).
  [B] delete the attestation guard -> `E Failed: DID NOT RAISE <class 'ValueError'>` (1 failed in 0.09s). DISCLOSED: guard [B] was FIRST SHIPPED UNGUARDED — a mutation proved deleting it left everything green — and its first test then passed for the WRONG reason (the fixture holds only beat sentences, whose stop_idx _sentences_from_json coerces, so the injection was a no-op). It now appends a GLUE line (source_id=GLUE_REFLECTION, stop_idx=99), the only shape that carries a foreign index through parsing.

VERIFICATION: make lint clean; tests/test_tour_authoring_gates.py 5 passed; tests/test_tour_certification_compose_replay.py 6 passed (the 5 direct call sites of the edited finalizer that the engine's judges flagged as never run for A5); make _test-python 2608 passed / 0 failed / exit 0 on an exclusive-container run. An earlier run of the same tree showed 1 error (test_seed.py, 50N42 'Unable to load NODE') caused by launching the suite while the engine still held the shared 7688 DB — a documented signature in this repo; the clean exclusive re-run confirms it.

RESIDUAL WEAKNESS, stated rather than hidden: I wrote the fix, wrote its test, and ran its own mutation check. That is self-blessing. The only independent check A5 received is the judge's re-derivation of artifact.py's contract and its own re-run of the pinned test. The structural remedy is inversion — real by default, tests opt into fakes — so a surface that configures nothing gets the real thing and fails loudly instead of silently serving canned output.
